Hi Jared —

Thanks for the sync today. Per our discussion, attaching the updated MAP draft (ACME_MAP_v2.pdf) that focuses the evaluation window and measurable success criteria for streaming chat generation. High-level plan:

- Evaluation window: Nov 8–12 (test runs and smoke + one production canary Nov 18)
- Scope: TTFT (time-to-first-token) and streaming incremental latency (per-token), concurrency sweep (1 / 16 / 64), sustained throughput (tokens/sec)
- Test model: redwood-chat-16k (quantized FP16 profile we discussed) on A100-80GB nodes
- Success benchmarks (initial targets): TTFT p95 < 500ms, per-token incremental p95 < 120ms, stable throughput scaling up to 16 concurrent live chats with target 40 tok/s per request

Action items:
1) Acme: confirm target user journeys and representative prompts (send a small set of 10–15 prompts).
2) Redwood: run baseline sweep and deliver a preliminary CSV of raw traces + summarized p50/p95/p99 by Nov 12.
3) Procurement/Legal: if procurement questionnaire is required, we can pause rolling canary until Nov 20.

CC'ing Vanessa and Ben to run the sweep and instrument extra tracing (per-request kv cache hit rates).

Subject: RE: MAP: baseline sweep results (prelim)

Attached are the raw traces and the summarized latency PDF (ttft_stream_results.csv, latency_summary.pdf). Key highlights from the Nov 8–12 sweep (short + long prompt mixes):

Test conditions summary:
- Model: redwood-chat-16k (FP16 quantized), generation length averaged 120 tokens (short) / 600 tokens (long)
- HW: A100-80GB, continuous batching enabled, batch timeout tuned to 6ms
- Dataset: 10 representative prompts from Acme (short) + 6 long clinical triage prompts provided by Jared

Aggregated results (short prompt, short generation target):
- Concurrency 1:
  - TTFT: p50 95ms, p95 240ms, p99 410ms
  - Per-token emission latency: p50 18ms, p95 62ms, p99 140ms
  - Throughput: 46 tok/s (single request steady-state)

- Concurrency 16:
  - TTFT: p50 130ms, p95 360ms, p99 760ms
  - Per-token emission latency: p50 22ms, p95 78ms, p99 210ms
  - Aggregate throughput: 700 tok/s (approx 43 tok/s per active request)

- Concurrency 64 (burst profile):
  - TTFT: p50 420ms, p95 1.1s, p99 2.4s
  - Per-token emission latency: p50 38ms, p95 150ms, p99 520ms
  - Aggregate throughput: 2600 tok/s (saturated batching, elevated queuing observed)

Long prompt behavior (600 tokens) shows similar per-token emission numbers after initial warm-up; TTFT increases with generation context length by ~30–80ms on p95 in a few runs. KV-cache hit rate was near 92% on repeated-turn workflows we simulated.

Observations / recommendations:
- Short prompt p95 TTFT (240–360ms) comfortably meets your stated canary SLO of <500ms.
- Burst and very high concurrency (64) reveal longer tail (p95 over 1s) due to queueing and larger batch assembly; recommend canary at concurrency ceiling 16 for initial rollout, then step to 32 with throttling rules.
- Incremental token latency remains low (p95 < 120ms) up to concurrency 16 — good for chat UX.
- Next steps: deliver a concise MAP appendix with these results and an annotated canary playbook for Nov 18–20.

Ben Carter
Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
